note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: From the specialisation hypotheses to the SSH evidence, RouterInterp, and its results

nodes.name: Prior MoE analyses found no clear specialisation
nodes.description: Prior work analysing MoE models has struggled to recover clear, interpretable patterns of expert specialisation, e.g. Mixtral shows no obvious topic-based expert assignment.

nodes.name: More micro-domains than experts
nodes.description: Real-world data contains far more fine-grained categories (micro-domains) than an MoE layer has experts (typically 8 to 128), so by the Pigeonhole Principle multiple micro-domains must be routed to the same expert.

nodes.name: DSH versus SSH predictions
nodes.description: The Domain Specialisation Hypothesis predicts an expert covers semantically similar micro-domains explainable by a single concept, while the Superposed Specialisation Hypothesis predicts experts cover semantically disjoint micro-domains that can only be explained by multiple concepts.

nodes.name: Interference-minimisation argument
nodes.description: Following superposition theory, rarely co-activated, dissimilar domains interfere little when sharing an expert, so the router is incentivised to co-locate dissimilar domains, letting an expert perform computation in superposition.

nodes.name: Load-balancing argument
nodes.description: With a load-balancing loss and small batches containing few macro-domains, the router is pushed to spread tokens of one macro-domain across experts, encouraging routing of dissimilar inputs to the same expert, contrary to the DSH.

nodes.name: SAE latents predict routing
nodes.description: SAE latents predict expert selection far more accurately than token co-occurrence statistics or sparse linear probes, reaching macro-F1 0.73 for routing prediction on gpt-oss-20b, and serve as feature-level proxies for micro-domains.

nodes.name: Experts span many semantic clusters
nodes.description: Clustering the explanations of each expert's top-20 predictive SAE latents gives mean 10.8 clusters on OLMoE-1B-7B (layer 15) and 11.3 on gpt-oss-20b (layer 20), far above the DSH prediction of 1 but below random assignment (about 16.6).

nodes.name: Evidence supports the SSH
nodes.description: Because expert-predictive latents fall in many distinct clusters, routing is explained only by multiple semantically disjoint micro-domains, supporting the SSH over the DSH, though experts retain some thematic coherence.

nodes.name: RouterInterp method
nodes.description: RouterInterp selects the top-45 SAE features per expert by approximated ablation effect, collects contexts where each feature and the expert are active (routed vs non-routed), and prompts an LLM explainer to synthesise a single prose explanation merging overlapping patterns.

nodes.name: Detection-style scoring
nodes.description: Explanations are scored by an LLM scorer predicting whether held-out windows (15 positive, 85 negative per expert) contain tokens routed to the expert, reported as F1, with human-LLM agreement comparable to human-human agreement.

nodes.name: RouterInterp beats baselines
nodes.description: RouterInterp reaches mean F1 0.492 on gpt-oss-20b and 0.602 on OLMoE-1B-7B versus 0.383 and 0.305 for Expert Impact AutoInterp and 0.299 and 0.342 for Unigram Lookup, winning at every layer (about 65% over Unigram Lookup on gpt-oss-20b).

nodes.name: SAE decomposition is the key ingredient
nodes.description: Verbalising token statistics only modestly helps (0.35 to 0.42) and full activating windows give 0.417; bigram explanations are narrow (P 0.39/R 0.59) and window explanations broad (P 0.30/R 0.81), while grouping evidence by SAE feature improves both (P 0.47/R 0.64).

nodes.name: Performance depends on SAE quality
nodes.description: Layer 16 of gpt-oss-20b has the worst SAE reconstruction (FVU 0.19-0.23) and weakest routing prediction, and RouterInterp performance correlates with SAE reconstruction quality across layers.

isolated_nodes.name: Apparent domain specialisation is compatible
isolated_nodes.description: Findings such as pruning half the experts for code generation or language-specific experts show an expert participates in a language or task, not that it does only that.

isolated_nodes.name: Functional-similarity hypothesis
isolated_nodes.description: Experts may group inputs by functional similarity (similar downstream transformations) rather than input similarity, a hypothesis for future work.

isolated_nodes.name: Expert Impact AutoInterp is volatile
isolated_nodes.description: Expert Impact AutoInterp does not beat plain activating windows (0.383 vs 0.417) and on OLMoE-1B-7B scores below Unigram Lookup (0.305 vs 0.342), with 19% of expert descriptions scoring exactly zero.

isolated_nodes.name: Evaluated on two models only
isolated_nodes.description: Evaluation covers only OLMoE-1B-7B and gpt-oss-20b in the 1B-20B range, and explanations grow longer as more features are aggregated.

isolated_nodes.name: MoE sparsity gives efficiency
isolated_nodes.description: Sparse MoE models activate only 2-15% of parameters per input, enabling large parameter scaling with minimal increases in inference cost.

structural_reasoning: Hypothesis formulation and theoretical motivation lead to SAE-based evidence for SSH, which motivates RouterInterp and its evaluation. Caveats and side discussion isolated.
